newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Kuehbacher would welcome Italy ERM re-entry.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Kuehbacher would welcome Italy ERM re-entry.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher said on Friday he would welcome Italy's rejoining the European Rate Mechanism (ERM) in a bid to join Europe's currency union and regretted that Britain was not taking similar steps.

He called Italy's effort to rejoin the ERM, which it was forced out of in September 1992, a natural step. Kuehbacher said "whoever wants to be a member of the currency union must be a member of the ERM for two years before joining the union, and I only regret that Britain is not taking the same steps."

But Kuehbacher, also president of the state central bank in Berlin, Brandenburg and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, declined to comment on the the date when Italy may rejoin, saying only that whenever the step is taken, it would be acceptable.
He also declined to speculate on whether Italy will actually be among the first nations to join the union in 1999, when it is expected to be launched.

A senior source said on the fringes of the congress that Italy has requested that the European Union monetary committee meet this weekend. That would allow Italy to table a proposal for re-entry to the exchange rate mechanism.
The Italian lira crashed out of the ERM in 1992 after coming under severe pressure from speculators.
But there has been persistent talk this year that a re-entry is imminent, particularly as the year-end draws closer.

Although there has been no clear ruling on this, it is generally assumed that reentry before the start of 1997 would give Italy better cards for participation in European Economic and Monetary Union, due to start in 1999.
One condition for entry to EMU is that a country's currency must have been trading steadily within the ERM's trading bands for at least two years.
